newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreigners bought $2 bln Russian bills in April.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners bought $2 bln Russian bills in April.

text.p: Non-residents invested $2 billion in the Russian government securities market in April, bringing the total since August last year to $11 billion, Konstantin Korishchenko, head of the Central Bank's open-market operations department, said on Thursday.
Korishchenko told a CS First Boston investment conference that there had been practically no outflow of non-resident funds from the market.

"This is because of continuing restrictions in carrying out forward contracts and because foreign investors still feel comfortable with interest rates a little higher than 30 percent a year in roubles," he said.
Non-residents now hold about 20 percent of the Russian government securities market, whose volume is $45-50 billion, Korishchenko said.
But foreigners already account for twice as much of the daily turnover on the market as Russian investors, he said.
Average daily turnover by foreign investors is $20-50 million, while Russian investors trade $10-20 million. The liquidity demands of the two groups vary.
This large involvement is already making it harder for the authorities to manage the market, especially as the market is effectively divided into two segments -- taxed and tax-free paper, he said.

Most foreign investors, enjoying the protection of double-taxation treaties, prefer to invest in the T-bills and bonds issued since February which are liable to the new tax. Russian investors prefer the older tax-exempt issues.
Korishchenko said the authorities were continuing to liberalise foreign access to the market, but would retain the ability to limit foreign capital inflows.

The Central Bank has announced a staged liberalisation of the market, which will remove all restrictions on foreigners repatriating profits from the government securities market by the end of the year.
